First a bit of background.

Why were cluster bombs invented? To take out massed armour - basically in the Cold War the US thought NATO would be heavily outnumbered by Warsaw Pact armour. To even things up they invented cluster bombs that are devastating when dropped on massed armour. The individual bomblets are each able to destroy an armoured vehicle if they hit it.

So what's the problem? Well early cluster bombs have a 'dudding rate' of a few percent (5% according to the manufacturer, up to 8% according to anti mine NGOs). So if you drop a bomb containing 166 submunitions a few will fail to detonate. If civilians cross the battlefield these can act like landmines. In Vietnam, Cambodia etc the vast amount of ordinance dropped makes this a serious problem. In Desert Storm the US dropped 10035 CBU-87s each containing 202 submunitions. A 5% dud rate gives 10035*202*0.05=101353 unexploded submunitions.

Now having said that the article seems a bit misinformed. The weapon the Saudis used is a sensor fused munition. These are fired over the battlefield. If they fly over a tank they fire and destroy it but they have a low dudding rate

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBU-97_Sensor_Fuzed_Weapon

The 40 Skeets scan an area of 1,500 by 500 feet (460 m × 150 m) using infrared and laser sensors, seeking targets by pattern-matching. When a Skeet finds a target it fires an explosively-formed penetrator to destroy it. If a Skeet fails to find a target, it self-destructs 50 feet (15 m) above the ground; if this fails, a back-up timer disables the Skeet. These features are intended to avoid later civilian casualties from unexploded munitions, and result in an unexploded-ordnance rate of less than 1%.

I.e. they're designed to leave a clean battlefield with no unexploded ordinance. Incidentally the US will only export weapons with a dudding rate below 1%.
